title: Yangians, Quantum Affine Algebras, and Transfer Matrices

items.title: The type-A RTT Yangian in the rational i-normalization
items.statement: For N≥2 over C, define Y_i(gl_N) by formal RTT generators and R_N(x)=xI+iP_N, with the type-A matrix-unit and tensor conventions explicit.
items.strategy: Fix the field, rank, bases, matrix units, auxiliary legs, formal-series expansion, R-matrix, and proposed Hopf maps.
items.axiom_use: None; the definition uses explicit finite bases and formal algebraic generators.

sources.title: A. I. Molev, M. L. Nazarov, and G. I. Olshanski, Yangians and classical Lie algebras
A. P. Isaev, Lectures on Quantum Groups and Yang-Baxter Equations
F. Loebbert, Lectures on Yangian Symmetry

items.title: The RTT relation has an explicit component commutator form
items.statement: The two-auxiliary-leg matrix RTT relation is equivalent coefficientwise to x[t_ij(u),t_kl(v)]=i(t_kj(v)t_il(u)-t_kj(u)t_il(v)) for x=u-v.
items.strategy: Expand one explicit matrix entry of both sides in the two auxiliary bases and rearrange; prove the converse entrywise as well.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof is a finite matrix-entry calculation.

sources.title: A. I. Molev, M. L. Nazarov, and G. I. Olshanski, Yangians and classical Lie algebras

items.title: The RTT Yangian has its standard Hopf structure
items.statement: The matrix-product coproduct, counit, and formal matrix-inverse antipode are well-defined on the RTT quotient and satisfy the Hopf identities.
items.strategy: Check RTT for a product of two monodromies, prove coassociativity and counit coefficientwise, then derive the inverse RTT relation and antipode identities.
items.axiom_use: None; all identities are formal algebra and recursive matrix inversion.

sources.title: A. I. Molev, M. L. Nazarov, and G. I. Olshanski, Yangians and classical Lie algebras

items.title: Evaluation modules of the type-A RTT Yangian
items.statement: For each left gl_N-module W and a∈C, specify t_ij(u)=δ_ij-iρ(E_ij)/(u-a), including the dual-natural action and its polynomial Lax matrix.
items.strategy: State the candidate action with its formal expansion and identify the indexed dual basis and auxiliary Lax operator.
items.axiom_use: None; the module and its action are explicitly specified.

sources.title: A. I. Molev, M. L. Nazarov, and G. I. Olshanski, Yangians and classical Lie algebras

items.title: The gl_N evaluation formula satisfies RTT
items.statement: For every left gl_N-module and spectral shift, the evaluation formula satisfies every component RTT relation; the dual-natural action is verified directly.
items.strategy: Derive the component RTT relation, expand the proposed action, cancel quadratic terms, and use the matrix-unit bracket.
items.axiom_use: None; all calculations are explicit algebra on matrix units.

sources.title: A. I. Molev, M. L. Nazarov, and G. I. Olshanski, Yangians and classical Lie algebras

items.title: The rational i-normalization is the standard RTT normalization after rescaling
items.statement: The change z=iu converts R_i(x)=xI+iP to R_0(z)=zI-P and sends an evaluation shift a to ia.
items.strategy: Substitute u=-iz and v=-iw in the matrix relation and simplify the scalar factor and shifted denominator.
items.axiom_use: None; the result is an exact scalar substitution.

sources.title: A. I. Molev, M. L. Nazarov, and G. I. Olshanski, Yangians and classical Lie algebras

items.title: The type-A rational R-matrix satisfies Yang–Baxter and has exact singular parameters
items.statement: For every N≥2, R_N(x)=xI+iP_N satisfies the spectral Yang–Baxter equation; it is invertible off ±i, with exact symmetric/antisymmetric kernels and ranks at the exceptional values.
items.strategy: Use the exact shared C² carrier for N=2; for N≥3 verify permutation products on the explicit triple tensor basis and expand; diagonalize P_N for inverse and rank claims.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses explicit finite tensor bases and finite-dimensional linear algebra.

items.title: The rational R-matrix intertwines two fundamental evaluation orders
items.statement: R_N(a-b) intertwines the coproduct action on V_N^∨(a)⊗V_N^∨(b) with the opposite coproduct action, and is an isomorphism exactly off the two singular differences.
items.strategy: Write each coproduct action as the ordered product of its evaluation Lax matrices and specialize the three-leg Yang–Baxter identity.
items.axiom_use: None; the intertwiner is a finite-dimensional matrix and the proof is a polynomial identity.

items.title: Finite periodic fundamental evaluation chain and transfer matrix
items.statement: For finite m and arbitrary complex inhomogeneities, define the dual-natural quantum space, ordered fundamental monodromy, and untwisted ordinary auxiliary trace.
items.strategy: Fix the finite tensor space, indexed flip operators, site order, polynomial Lax operators, and trace convention.
items.axiom_use: None; all spaces and maps are finite and explicitly indexed.

items.title: The periodic fundamental monodromy satisfies RTT
items.statement: For the explicitly ordered finite monodromy, two auxiliary copies satisfy the RTT relation for every pair of complex spectral parameters.
items.strategy: Use the local three-leg Yang–Baxter relation, commute operators on distinct sites, and induct on the finite number of sites.
items.axiom_use: None; induction is on a finite natural number and each operator acts on an explicit finite tensor product.

items.title: Finite periodic transfer matrices commute
items.statement: The ordinary untwisted auxiliary traces commute for all spectral parameters and arbitrary finite-chain inhomogeneities, including singular differences by polynomial continuation.
items.strategy: Use the invertible auxiliary R-matrix away from ±i, trace the conjugation identity, then extend the finite polynomial commutator to all parameter pairs.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite matrix traces and the elementary polynomial identity principle over C.

items.title: The one-root gl2 Bethe equation cancels the unwanted transfer term
items.statement: Under the stated pseudovacuum eigenvalue hypotheses, the one-root condition a(v)=d(v) cancels the B(u)Ω term and makes a nonzero B(v)Ω a transfer-matrix eigenvector.
items.strategy: Extract the A-B and D-B commutation formulas from component RTT and apply them to the pseudovacuum.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof is a direct operator calculation in a representation.

title: Yangians, Quantum Affine Algebras, and Transfer Matrices: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: An explicit two-site periodic transfer matrix and permutation Hamiltonian
items.statement: For N=2, m=2 and equal shifts i/2, compute τ(u)=(2u²+1/2)I-P12 and the normalized logarithmic derivative H=P12-I.
items.strategy: Expand the two Lax factors, evaluate their three partial traces in matrix units, and compute the special value, derivative, and inverse.
items.axiom_use: None; all maps are explicit finite matrices.

sources.title: L. D. Faddeev, How Algebraic Bethe Ansatz Works for Integrable Model

items.title: A one-root Bethe equation need not produce a complete set of vectors
items.statement: On a two-dimensional direct sum of counit modules, every one-root scalar equation holds but every positive-root Bethe vector vanishes, so the Bethe vectors from the chosen pseudovacuum are incomplete.
items.strategy: Compute the counit action on each summand and explicitly determine the span of all root vectors.
items.axiom_use: None; this is an explicit two-dimensional counterexample.
